You are given a sequence of integers a=[a1,a2,…,an]%%ZSMJ1%% of length n%%ZSMJ2%%. Its subsequence is obtained by removing zero or more elements from the sequence a%%ZSMJ3%% (they do not necessarily go consecutively). For example, for the sequence a=[11,20,11,33,11,20,11]%%ZSMJ4%%:
Suppose that an additional non-negative integer k%%ZSMJ14%% (1≤k≤n%%ZSMJ15%%) is given, then the subsequence is called optimal if:
it has a length of k%%ZSMJ16%% and the sum of its elements is the maximum possible among all subsequences of length k%%ZSMJ17%%;
and among all subsequences of length k%%ZSMJ18%% that satisfy the previous item, it is lexicographically minimal.

Recall that the sequence b=[b1,b2,…,bk]%%ZSMJ19%% is lexicographically smaller than the sequence c=[c1,c2,…,ck]%%ZSMJ20%% if the first element (from the left) in which they differ less in the sequence b%%ZSMJ21%% than in c%%ZSMJ22%%. You are given a sequence of a=[a1,a2,…,an]%%ZSMJ35%% and m%%ZSMJ36%% requests, each consisting of two numbers kj%%ZSMJ37%% and posj%%ZSMJ38%% (1≤k≤n%%ZSMJ39%%, 1≤posj≤kj%%ZSMJ40%%). For each query, print the value that is in the index posj%%ZSMJ41%% of the optimal subsequence of the given sequence a%%ZSMJ42%% for k=kj%%ZSMJ43%%.

For example, if n=4%%ZSMJ44%%, a=[10,20,30,20]%%ZSMJ45%%, kj=2%%ZSMJ46%%, then the optimal subsequence is [20,30]%%ZSMJ47%% — it is the minimum lexicographically among all subsequences of length 2%%ZSMJ48%% with the maximum total sum of items. Thus, the answer to the request kj=2%%ZSMJ49%%, posj=1%%ZSMJ50%% is the number 20%%ZSMJ51%%, and the answer to the request kj=2%%ZSMJ52%%, posj=2%%ZSMJ53%% is the number 30%%ZSMJ54%%.
input: The first line contains an integer n%%ZSMJ55%% (1≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ56%%) — the length of the sequence a%%ZSMJ57%%.
The second line contains elements of the sequence a%%ZSMJ58%%: integer numbers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ59%% (1≤ai≤109%%ZSMJ60%%).
The third line contains an integer m%%ZSMJ61%% (1≤m≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ62%%) — the number of requests.
The following m%%ZSMJ63%% lines contain pairs of integers kj%%ZSMJ64%% and posj%%ZSMJ65%% (1≤k≤n%%ZSMJ66%%, 1≤posj≤kj%%ZSMJ67%%) — the requests.
output: Print m%%ZSMJ68%% integers r1,r2,…,rm%%ZSMJ69%% (1≤rj≤109%%ZSMJ70%%) one per line: answers to the requests in the order they appear in the input. The value of rj%%ZSMJ71%% should be equal to the value contained in the position posj%%ZSMJ72%% of the optimal subsequence for k=kj%%ZSMJ73%%.
